scenes.text: What would happen if the Sun suddenly disappeared?
For about eight minutes, nothing at all! That's how long sunlight takes to reach us.
Then, the sky would go black. Even the Moon would vanish, because moonlight is just reflected sunlight.
Plants would stop making food, and slowly start to die.
Without the Sun's pull, Earth would fly off in a straight line, into deep space.
But the biggest change would be the cold. In a week, it would be colder than any winter. Within a year, the oceans would freeze over.
Still, deep under the ice, tiny life could survive near warm volcanic vents.
So, thank you, Sun! Subscribe for more what-ifs.
What would happen if Earth slowly stopped spinning?
First, one day would last a whole year! Six months of sunshine, then six months of darkness.
The day side would bake under the Sun, while the night side would freeze solid.
The oceans would move too! Without the spin, water would slide toward the poles.
That would leave one giant continent, wrapped around the middle of the planet.
And the weather would totally change. Hurricanes couldn't form, because Earth's spin is what makes them swirl.
So, keep spinning, Earth! Subscribe for more what-ifs.
What would happen if all the bees suddenly disappeared?
First, lots of flowers would stop making seeds. Bees carry pollen from flower to flower.
Apples, almonds and blueberries would become rare and expensive. And no more honey!
Farmers would have to pollinate by hand, one flower at a time.
Animals that eat those fruits and seeds would go hungry too.
But we wouldn't starve. Wheat, rice and corn are pollinated by the wind.
Still, our meals would be way more boring. So, thank you, bees! Subscribe for more what-ifs.
What would happen if every tree on Earth suddenly disappeared?
First, don't panic. We'd still have oxygen! About half of it comes from tiny ocean plankton.
But trees soak up tons of carbon dioxide, so the planet would heat up faster.
Without roots to hold the ground, rain would wash the soil away.
Millions of animals, like owls and squirrels, would lose their homes.
And cities would get much hotter, with no shade to cool them down.
So, thank you, trees! Subscribe for more what-ifs.
What would happen if Earth had rings, just like Saturn?
First, the sky would look amazing! A huge glowing arch, stretching from one side of the sky to the other.
Right at the equator, though, you'd see them edge-on, as a thin line straight overhead.
The rings would also cast giant shadows, making some winters even colder.
At night, they'd reflect sunlight, so nights would never get fully dark.
But launching rockets would be tricky. Those rings are full of ice and rock!
So, would you want rings? Subscribe for more what-ifs.
What would happen if all the ice on Earth melted?
First, the oceans would rise about seventy meters. That's taller than a twenty-story building!
Lots of coastal cities would end up underwater, and every map would need redrawing.
Polar bears and penguins would lose their icy homes.
And without bright ice to bounce sunlight away, Earth would heat up even faster.
The good news? Melting all of it would take thousands of years.
So, thank you, ice! Subscribe for more what-ifs.
What would happen if all the oceans suddenly dried up?
First, it would almost stop raining. Most rain starts as ocean water that evaporates.
Rivers and lakes would dry out, turning the land into one giant desert.
Oceans keep temperatures steady, so days would be scorching, and nights freezing.
We'd also lose the plankton that make about half the oxygen we breathe.
On the bright side, you could walk down into the Mariana Trench. It's eleven kilometers deep!
So, thank you, oceans! Subscribe for more what-ifs.
What would happen if the dinosaurs never went extinct?
Sixty-six million years ago, a giant asteroid hit Earth. But imagine it missed!
Dinosaurs would keep ruling the planet, on every single continent.
Mammals, like our ancestors, would probably stay small, hiding in burrows.
So humans might never have appeared at all!
Fun fact: birds actually are dinosaurs. So some dinos did survive!
So, thank you... asteroid? Subscribe for more what-ifs.
What would happen if friction suddenly disappeared?
First, you couldn't walk. Your shoes need friction to push against the ground.
You couldn't hold anything, either. Your pencil would just slip right out of your hand.
Knots would untie, and screws would slide right out of the walls.
Car wheels would spin, without moving the car at all.
And anything already moving would just keep sliding, forever!
So, thank you, friction! Subscribe for more what-ifs.
What would happen if Earth was twice as big?
If it were made of the same stuff, gravity would be twice as strong!
You'd feel twice as heavy, and you could only jump half as high.
Trees and animals would grow shorter and sturdier, to carry their weight.
Mountains couldn't get as tall, either. They'd crumble under their own weight.
But the biggest change? Escaping to space would be way harder. Rockets would need to be enormous!
So, thank you, Earth, for being just the right size! Subscribe for more what-ifs.
